extracted.intended_audience: business administration faculty, curriculum planners, and students (those designing or taking grant-writing courses)
extracted.subtask_description: A proposed undergraduate/graduate business-administration course curriculum and instructional units for teaching grant-writing skills, including the parts of proposals, budgeting, evaluation design, alignment with funder criteria, and submission procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal as a marketing document
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant proposals should be viewed as marketing documents; those documents that sell their ideas to the grant reviewers are the proposals that are funded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand grant reviewers as gatekeepers (e.g., NSF used 54,000 reviewers for 40,000 proposals). Write persuasively to 'sell' the idea to reviewers; focus on clarity, relevance, and persuasive presentation of need and solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include standard parts of a grant application
rubrics_metrics.description: Most grant applications contain an Abstract, Introduction, Problem Statement, Objectives, Plan-of-action/Method/Program/Proposal, Evaluation, Future Necessary Funding, Budget, and Cover Letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review and define the parts of most grant applications, examine various grant samples, and ensure the proposal contains the required sections. Course instruction should review samples and specify which sections are required for assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align proposal to funder criteria and agency needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Review grant criteria; identify and select potential funding source; define and identify agency needs and articulate concerns, issues, needs, and problems into problem statement(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research funders to determine their priorities and application criteria; tailor the problem statement and objectives to the funder’s stated needs; use funder selection to inform project scope and language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem statement clarity and articulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Articulate concerns, issues, needs, and problems into clear problem statement(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use established criteria to critique and edit problem statements; ensure the problem statement is specific, evidence-based, and framed so that objectives and methods logically follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful and measurable objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Compose meaningful and measurable objectives for a problem statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objectives should be specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound (measurable outcomes linked to the problem). Ensure objectives connect directly to the problem statement and to evaluation measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy, methods, and solution approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a strategy, method, and/or a solution approach to a problem statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe feasible methods and an actionable plan-of-action that logically achieve stated objectives; separate methods (means) from goals (ends) and justify methodological choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation design and assessment criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop criteria for assessing the problem statement, including summative evaluation and comprehensive evaluation design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design an evaluation plan that specifies data sources, measures, timing, and how results will be used; organize evaluation information and connect evaluation results to objectives (summative assessment). Use evaluation criteria to choose methods and budget items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal continuity and logical structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain proposal continuity - connect problem statement with objectives; review logical structure; separate means from ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all sections follow logically, with objectives derived from the problem statement and methods and evaluation aligned to objectives. Edit for flow and coherence so reviewers can easily follow the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnerships and collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and describe partnership and collaboration as part of the proposal where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articulate roles, contributions, and formal agreements with partners; demonstrate how partnerships strengthen feasibility, sustainability, or scope to funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of criteria to critique and edit
rubrics_metrics.description: Use defined criteria to critique problem statements, budgets, evaluation design, and other proposal elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach and apply checklists/criteria to iteratively review and improve proposal components; peer critique and instructor rubrics should target alignment, clarity, feasibility, and funder fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget accuracy and completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop estimate of cost and prepare budget including budget format, budget summary, budget detail, fringe benefits, personnel, budget checklist, and match (if required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide correct costing and justifications for each budget line; follow funder-specified budget formats; include fringe calculations, personnel allocations, and documentation of matching funds when applicable. Use the budget checklist to verify completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget justification and linkage to evaluation/strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Use criteria to critique, edit and select evaluation design and strategy; justify budget items in relation to proposed methods and evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure each budget item is tied to a task or objective and that evaluation costs are included. Reviewers expect that budgets reflect the proposed work and demonstrate cost-effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract and cover letter quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare an effective introduction, proposal abstract (summary), and cover letter; ensure quality of key personnel is communicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract and cover letter should succinctly summarize significance, objectives, and requested funding; highlight key personnel qualifications and roles. Use critiquing criteria to refine these elements for clarity and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address scoring criteria and neglected scoring items
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware of score sheets and neglected scoring items; use simulation grant scoring to train applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify typical reviewer scoring categories and explicitly address them in the proposal. Conduct mock reviews and score simulations to uncover commonly neglected items and refine the application accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow proposal organization, review preparation, and submission guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow guidelines for review preparation and submission; understand what funders are looking for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere strictly to funder formatting, page limits, submission systems, deadlines, and required attachments. Organize materials so reviewers can readily locate required information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative analysis and revision of applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze grant application materials using the course criteria and revise accordingly before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple rounds of review, peer feedback, and instructor edits to refine the proposal. Emphasize revising for clarity, alignment with funder priorities, and responsiveness to scoring rubrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use real-world community organizations and team-based projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Students select community organization and program area for grant preparation; working teams formed for grant preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground assignments in real organizational needs to increase relevance and provide practical experience. Teams should engage with community partners and produce a fundable proposal as a course deliverable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission and administrative completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete and submit the grant application per funder procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm all attachments, signatures, and submission steps are complete prior to deadline; simulate the submission process in class to avoid procedural errors.
